newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka's capital has 100 days to clean up.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's capital has 100 days to clean up.

text.p: The new mayor of the Sri Lankan capital has called on residents to rid the city of its mountains of garbage within 100 days.
The state-owned Observer newspaper said on Thursday the Colombo Municipal Council (CMC) was launching a 100-day crash programme to tidy up the image of the city once known as the "Garden of Asia".
Mayor Karu Jayasuriya said the CMC will spruce up public parks, playgrounds, markets and other public places and remove thousands of posters covering the city's walls, the newspaper reported.

He asked residents to help authorities clean the city by joining a special day-long effort next month. Jayasuriya said several non-governmental organisations, women's organisations and schools have promised to lend him a helping hand.
The clean-up campaign begins on June 7.
"The garbage problem is the biggest problem," Jayasuriya was quoted as saying by the paper after residents complained of a mosquito menace caused by garbage lying on streets.
Colombo's population has risen sharply in recent years to about 800,000. The city generates 800 tonnes of garbage each day, making collection difficult for the cash-strapped council.
The CMC recently acquired nearly 100 garbage collection trucks under a Japanese grant and since then has been trying hard to rid the city of its stinking refuse.
